# How to Set Up a WhatsApp Catalog for Your Malaysian Business (2026 Step-by-Step Guide)

Setting up a WhatsApp Catalog takes under 15 minutes and costs nothing: download WhatsApp Business, tap Business Tools then Catalog, add each product with a photo and RM price, then share your catalog link in any chat. No website, no WhatsApp Business API, and no developer needed to get started.

## Why This Matters More Than a Website for Many Malaysian SMEs

WhatsApp is where Malaysian customers already are — message open rates on the platform regularly run above 95%, far higher than email or even Instagram DMs. For a home baker in Subang Jaya or a phone case seller in Johor Bahru, building a full e-commerce website before making a single sale often does not make sense. A WhatsApp Catalog lets you showcase products with photos, prices, and descriptions inside the same chat window customers already use to ask "got stock or not?" — without them ever leaving the app. It also supports Malay, Mandarin, and English product listings, which matters for Malaysia's mixed-language customer base. Because it runs on a phone you already own and needs no hosting, domain, or monthly subscription, it is usually the very first digital storefront a Malaysian micro-business ever builds — often before a Facebook Shop, Shopee listing, or website exists at all.

If you are still deciding between building a full website or relying on WhatsApp and social media, [our comparison guide on website vs social media for small businesses](/blog/bisnes-kecil-malaysia-perlu-website-atau-media-sosial-2026) walks through when each makes sense.

## Before You Start: What You Need

- The free **WhatsApp Business app** (separate from your personal WhatsApp — do not use your personal number)
- A dedicated business phone number, ideally one customers already recognise
- Clear product photos (a phone camera in good lighting is enough — no studio needed)
- Prices in RM and a one-line description for each product

## Step-by-Step: Setting Up Your WhatsApp Catalog

**1. Download and register WhatsApp Business.** Available free on the Play Store and App Store. Register with your business number, not your personal one.

**2. Complete your Business Profile.** Add your business name, category, address (or service area), operating hours, and a short description. This appears above your catalog and builds trust before a customer even messages you.

**3. Open Business Tools, then tap Catalog.** This is where you will add and manage every product.

**4. Add your first product.** Upload a photo, enter the product name, price in RM, a short description, and an optional product code or link. Repeat for each item — most sellers start with their 5–10 best sellers rather than the full range.

**5. Organise with categories (optional but recommended).** If you sell more than 10–15 items, group them (e.g. "Kek Coklat", "Kek Buah", "Custom Order") so customers can browse faster instead of scrolling through everything.

**6. Turn on the Cart feature if you want in-chat ordering.** Customers can add multiple items to a cart and send you the full order in one message, instead of listing items one by one in chat.

**7. Test your catalog link before sharing it publicly.** Tap the catalog, then Share, and send the link to your own second device or a colleague to confirm every photo and price loads correctly.

## How to Share Your Catalog With Customers

Once it is live, get it in front of people through more than one channel: pin the catalog link in your WhatsApp Business profile so it shows automatically when someone opens a chat with you; generate a QR code (built into the app) for printed menus, receipts, or a table tent at a physical stall; post it to your WhatsApp Status, which works like an Instagram Story but reaches contacts who already messaged you before; and add the link to your Instagram and Facebook bio. If you are running [Meta ads](/blog/how-to-know-facebook-ads-working-malaysia-roas-2026), a click-to-WhatsApp ad that opens directly into your catalog usually converts better than sending traffic to a generic landing page, since the customer can browse and ask questions in the same window.

## 5 Mistakes That Quietly Kill Catalog Conversions

1. **Blurry or inconsistent photos** — a catalog with five different photo styles looks unmanaged, even if the products themselves are good.
2. **Missing prices.** "WhatsApp for price" listings frustrate browsers who wanted to compare before messaging — most will simply leave.
3. **Out-of-stock items left up.** Nothing kills trust faster than a customer messaging about something that sold out two weeks ago.
4. **No clear next step.** Every product description should make it obvious what to do next — "Reply with your size and address to order."
5. **Never updating it.** A catalog set up once in January and never touched again stops reflecting your actual best sellers or current promotions.
6. **Ignoring the description field.** Leaving it blank wastes space that could answer the two or three questions every buyer asks anyway — size, material, delivery time — before they even open the chat.

## When a Free Catalog Isn't Enough: Moving to the WhatsApp Business API

The free WhatsApp Business app comfortably handles one phone, one person replying, and a catalog of a reasonable size. It starts to strain once you need multiple staff replying from shared numbers, automated order confirmations, or a catalog synced directly with your inventory system. That is the point to consider the WhatsApp Business API, which requires an official provider and carries per-message costs. We break down exactly what that costs in Malaysia in our [WhatsApp Business API pricing guide](/blog/whatsapp-business-api-pricing-malaysia-2026), and how SMEs use it for automation in our [WhatsApp Business API automation guide](/blog/whatsapp-business-api-malaysia-sme-automation-2026).

## A Quick Example: A Home Bakery in Subang Jaya

A home-based bakery in Subang Jaya used to take orders entirely through free-form chat — customers would ask for photos and prices individually, and the owner spent close to an hour every evening just retyping the same answers. After setting up a WhatsApp Catalog with 12 core items, clear RM prices, and the Cart feature switched on, most customers started browsing and sending a complete order in one message. The owner estimated it cut daily order-handling time by roughly half, without spending anything on a website or app.

## Getting More From Your Catalog: Photos, Ads, and Traffic

A catalog is only as strong as what goes into it. Product photos that look properly lit and consistent tend to convert noticeably better than phone snapshots taken in different lighting each time, and pairing the catalog with even a small Meta ads budget sending people straight into a click-to-WhatsApp flow can turn a quiet catalog into a steady stream of enquiries. faq.q: Do I need the WhatsApp Business API to set up a catalog?
faq.a: No. The free WhatsApp Business app includes the Catalog feature — you only need the paid API once you require multiple agents, automation, or CRM integration.

faq.q: How many products should I add to my WhatsApp Catalog when starting out?
faq.a: Start with your 5–10 best sellers rather than a full range. A focused catalog with clear photos and prices converts better than an overwhelming, half-finished one.

faq.q: Can customers order directly through my WhatsApp Catalog?
faq.a: Yes — turning on the Cart feature lets customers add multiple items and send the full order as one message instead of listing products individually in chat.

faq.q: Why is my WhatsApp Catalog not getting any orders?
faq.a: The most common causes are missing prices, blurry inconsistent photos, or out-of-stock items still listed — all of which make browsers leave before messaging you.

faq.q: Does a WhatsApp Catalog work if I sell in Malay, Mandarin, and English?
faq.a: Yes, product names and descriptions can be written in any language, which is why many Malaysian sellers list items in mixed Malay-English or Mandarin-English for their customer base.
